name: Yang dimension
description: Yang dimension over the default coefficient field $\mathbb F_2$ (that is, $\mathrm Y_2$)
definition: The **Yang Dimension** in this catalogue is the characteristic-two specialization $\mathrm{Y}(\mathcal H)=\mathrm{Y}_2(\mathcal H)$: the projective dimension, over $\mathbb F_2$, of its associated ideal $I^*_{\mathcal H}$; equivalently, the length of a minimal free resolution over $\mathbb F_2$. Characteristic zero gives a lower bound $\mathrm Y_0\leq\mathrm Y_2$. The homological formula permits exceptions at torsion primes, but no explicit Boolean class separating $\mathrm Y_2$ from another characteristic is currently recorded.
graph_summary: Default characteristic-two value: $\mathrm Y=\mathrm Y_2$, the minimal-resolution length of the associated ideal. It is at least $\mathrm Y_0$.
comments: The characteristic-$p$ entry denotes a family of fixed-prime parameters. The default node is its $p=2$ specialization, not a field-independent invariant.

monotonic.proof: Yang's full version \cite{yang2018homological} exhibits the delta class on $2^d$ inputs as a subfamily of the conjunction class, with homological dimensions $2^d-1$ and $d+1$, respectively. For $d\geq3$ this reverses the asserted subfamily-monotonic inequality.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

p_monotonic.proof: Yang proves that restricting the domain (projection) cannot increase the projective dimension of the canonical ideal.
